title: 'Sharpness' of (S3)+(S4) is asserted but the converse is not proved

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: moderate (an over-claimed "sharpness").**

Proposition "An arbitrary monotone collapse breaks the triangle inequality" exhibits ONE monotone $v$ on $M_2$ ($v(a)=v(b)=2/3$, triangle $(a,\top,b)$ giving $1>2/3$) that violates the triangle inequality. The critic confirmed this example numerically. From it, the Abstract, Remark "precise dichotomy", and Theorem "main" conclude that the state law is **sharp** and "(S3) together with $\&$-subadditivity (S4) is exactly the additional structure required."

This is an over-reading. A single counterexample shows (S3) **cannot simply be dropped**; it does NOT establish that (S3)+(S4) are **necessary** — i.e. that any monotone collapse yielding the integral pseudometric for all formulas must satisfy (S3) and (S4). The words "sharp" and "exact additional ingredient" assert a converse that is not proved.

**Required fix.** Prove the converse, e.g.: assume the integral pseudometric holds for all theories over $L$ with a fixed full-support product measure; by specializing to constant formulas ($\bar\varphi(a)\equiv x$, etc.) deduce the pointwise triangle inequality for all $x,y,z\in L$, and from it derive (S3) (accessing $\vee,\wedge$ via $\leftrightarrow$ with $\top$) and (S4) (via $\odot$). Absent such a derivation, downgrade "sharp/exact" to "cannot be dropped".
